# `packslip verify`

- **Usage:** `packslip verify [FLAGS] <BUNDLE>`

Verify a packslip, or a release list, against a pinned identity or key

Check the signature, log evidence, and statement structure. With --artifact, also check local files against signed digests and artifact sizes. Without it, only the bundle is checked. Nothing is downloaded: remote artifacts and linked provenance are not fetched.

Choose what to trust. By default, the identity policy comes from the project the document claims, if it is on github.com or gitlab.com: that forge's issuer and a certificate that records that repository as its source, whichever workflow signed, so a reusable workflow of another repository may sign (a certificate that records no source must come from a workflow of that repository). Any other project needs --pubkey or an identity flag. For a keyless release, --issuer with --identity-prefix (any workflow of a repository, such as https://github.com/owner/repo/) or --identity (one certificate identity, including its ref) pins the signer. --issuer with --source-repository instead pins the repository the certificate must record as its source, whichever workflow signed: unlike an identity prefix of that repository, it also matches a reusable workflow of another repository. In --identity, --identity-prefix, and --source-repository, a github.com or gitlab.com repository's name matches in any letter case, as the forge resolves it; the rest, such as a workflow's path and ref, matches exactly. For a key-signed release, pass --pubkey. --pin adds a check on top of the identity policy: the signing repository must have that signer fingerprint.

For a GitHub or GitLab project, the identity flags narrow what the project's name requires and never replace it: the run that signed must match the flags and still belong to the project's repository, so --issuer alone accepts only that repository's workflows and the reusable workflows it calls. To verify a document signed outside the project's repository, such as a repackager's, name its signer with --issuer and --identity, --identity-prefix, or --source-repository, and add --allow-other-repository. For any other project, the flags you pass are the whole policy: there, --issuer alone accepts any signer from that issuer.

Then match the verified project and version to what you meant to install. For a release list, the command does not check the expiry or compare the sequence with an earlier list. See https://packslip.dev/docs/verifying/.

## Arguments
- **`<BUNDLE>`** — Local release bundle or signed release list to verify

## Flags
- **`-a --artifact <ARTIFACT>`** — A downloaded artifact or resource asset to check against the bundle, matched by file name, so keep the name it was published under (repeatable)
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

## Trust
- **`-p --pubkey <PUBKEY>`** — The pinned public key file, or its base64 line
- **`--identity <IDENTITY>`** — The certificate identity a keyless signer must have, including its ref, such as https://github.com/owner/repo/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v1.2.3; a GitHub or GitLab repository name in it matches in any case
- **`--identity-prefix <IDENTITY_PREFIX>`** — A prefix the certificate identity must start with, such as https://github.com/owner/repo/; a GitHub or GitLab repository name in it matches in any case
- **`--issuer <ISSUER>`** — The OIDC issuer a keyless signer must have; pass it with --identity or --identity-prefix, since for a project not on GitHub or GitLab it alone accepts any signer from that issuer
- **`--source-repository <SOURCE_REPOSITORY>`** — The repository the signing certificate must record as its source, such as https://github.com/owner/repo, whichever workflow signed, so it also matches a reusable workflow of another repository, which an identity prefix of the repository does not. Needs --issuer, and replaces --identity and --identity-prefix
- **`--pin <PIN>`** — The signer fingerprint (ps1_...) the certificate's repository must have, as `packslip pin` prints it
- **`--allow-other-repository`** — Accept a keyless signer outside the repository a GitHub or GitLab project names, such as a repackager's; needs --issuer, and --identity, --identity-prefix, or --source-repository to name that signer
- **`--allow-unlogged`** — Accept a bundle without a transparency log entry
- **`--trusted-root <TRUSTED_ROOT>`** — A sigstore trusted_root.json to use instead of the embedded one

## Output
- **`-J --json`** — Print the verified report as JSON, including every listed artifact with its signed digest and source_repository when the signing certificate records one; for a release list, print the verified list statement

## Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | The bundle verified, and every --artifact matched it |
| `1` | Verification failed, or an input was unusable: a file could not be read, a key or fingerprint is malformed, or the trust flags conflict or are missing |
| `2` | The command line is invalid |

## Examples

**Verify a GitHub release against its repository**

```
packslip verify packslip.sigstore.json \
        --identity-prefix https://github.com/owner/repo/ \
        --issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
        --artifact mytool-1.2.3-linux-x64.tar.gz
```

**Verify hk 2.3.0 against its signer fingerprint**

```
packslip verify packslip.sigstore.json \
        --pin ps1_snirenkjwr7m5ozgcufameodnm \
        --artifact hk-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
```

**Verify a key-signed release**

```
packslip verify packslip.sigstore.json \
        --pubkey release.pub \
        --artifact mytool-1.2.3-linux-x64.tar.gz
```
